{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Nigeria|Cuisine of Nigeria]]

'''Ẹba''' is a popular Nigerian [[Cookbook:Swallow|swallow]] made from cassava flakes (garri)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nigerian Eba |url=https://www.seriouseats.com/nigerian-eba-5270376 |access-date=2023-12-26 |website=Serious Eats |language=en}}</ref> and is eaten with various soups, such as [[Cookbook:Egusi Soup|ẹgusi]], [[Cookbook:Efo Riro (Nigerian Amaranth Soup)|ẹfọ riro]], and [[Cookbook:Ogbono Soup|ọgbọnọ soup]]. It is starchy and considered a heavy food.

==Ingredients==

*1 [[Cookbook:Liter|liter]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Units of measurement#Nigeria|milk tins]] of processed [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava]] flakes (garri)

== Equipment ==

*Wooden spatula
*Pot

==Procedure==

#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] water in a pot.
#Gradually stir in the cassava flour, and cook until it forms a smooth [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
#Serve with your [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] of choice.
